results.title: Best Exa Alternatives: Features and Pricing Compared
results.content:
Fast SERP returns Google’s top 10 organic results, faster than a full results page. The SERP API also covers Google Images.
 Deep Lookup, a beta product in the Bright Data dashboard, is the closest match to Exa Websets. A “Find all” query builds a list of companies or people, and Enrichment mode (“For each”) fills new columns for a list. Each row carries source links and confidence indicators.
 Business Search, also in beta, searches people and company records with structured conditions or a plain-language sentence.
 Scraper Studio builds custom scrapers from a plain-English description. Its templates include Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar scrapers for paper data, and Sitemap scrapers that list every URL in a site’s sitemap. [...] Parallel’s Search API takes a natural-language objective together with short keyword queries and returns LLM-ready excerpts in Markdown rather than whole pages. Extract returns the full content of a URL. Its other APIs mirror Exa’s Agent, Websets and Monitors: Task for research, FindAll for entity lists and Monitor for tracking.

results.title: Exa's Websets V2 Runs 4x Faster at Half the Cost for Web Research | AlphaSignal
results.content:
## Websets takes on agent loops

Exa evaluated V2 on two internal benchmarks, Company FindAll and People FindAll. Each benchmark contains 20 complex queries, and a result counts only when it satisfies the stated criteria. The comparison included Websets, Claude Code, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Parallel FindAll, reflecting the common alternative of repeatedly sending a general-purpose agent through search and verification steps.

| Benchmark | Queries | Verified matches | Matches per query | Cost per match |
------
| Company FindAll | 20 | 514 | 25.7 | $0.024 |
| People FindAll | 20 | 613 | 30.65 | $0.0169 | [...] - Exa released Websets V2: 4x faster dataset building at roughly half the cost per match.
- Accuracy and recall are up 20%, and the gains apply automatically for all users with no code changes.
- The subscription is gone; pricing is now $0.10 per compute unit plus $5 per 1,000 searches.
- Every usage-plan user gets API access, billed from the same credits as Exa's Search API.
- On Exa's own benchmarks, V2 averaged $0.017 to $0.024 per verified match versus Claude Code, Gemini, and Parallel.
- Existing Starter and Pro users must opt in to the new pricing, and the switch can't be undone. [...] At Exa's reported benchmark rates, 300 verified people matches would cost about $5.07, while 300 company matches would cost about $7.20 before additional enrichment and workload-specific variation. Teams replacing a custom search-agent loop can compare both systems on the same queries, using cost per valid row, coverage, latency, and citation quality as the decision criteria.
